rationale: J9 (2026-09-30). Pins BOTH directions of the private-name rule, because the cheap fix is to delete the whole pass-3 guess branch and that would remove 44 rows of honest 0.5 suspicion. A `#name` is class-scoped in JavaScript — installed on each instance at construction, never on the prototype — so it can neither be declared by a base nor shadowed by a subclass. The lane emitted six such rows across the full corpus (URLSearchParams.#update_url, Map.#read_all, Map.#source, Set.#init, Set.#source, Date.#init); Date's only override edge was a private field, so the rule removes that base entirely. The forbid rows are what make this load-bearing: the edge COUNT is unchanged if the guard is replaced by a blanket suppression of the branch, and only naming the bad rows catches that.

expectRelationships.note: a PUBLIC method against a base not declared in this file stays, at the 0.5 first-parent-guess tier — Map really does have `get`, so this is honest suspicion rather than a fabrication

forbidRelationships.note: a private FIELD: class-scoped, never a prototype member
a private METHOD, so the rule is not merely about the field shape
